text:
incident-bot: ALERT — elevated 5xx rate and timeouts observed from pra1 (prairies-1) edge pool. 5m error rate = 6.8% (baseline 0.2%). Auto-escalation to #incidents triggered.

Amol: seeing a correlated spike in upstream 502s to proxy-router in pra1. Also increased TCP RSTs on egress. Not seeing saturation on GPU pools.

Kate (SRE): confirming, dashboards show gateway 502/504s from edge-proxy instances ~15:07 UTC. Rolling error map shows concentrated traffic from a handful of POPs in pra1.

Devon (Platform): gate: is this the new http/keepalive change we rolled yesterday?

Amol: possible. Kernel-level keepalive tweak went live in pra1 at 14:50 UTC. I'm pulling logs now.

Maria (Support): we already have two customers flagging increased failures for embed and generate endpoints, reported ~15:20 UTC. Ticket numbers: #12345, #12346. They see immediate 502s.

Kate (SRE): quick triage plan: 1) throttle new long-running requests at LB (lower max in-flight) 2) add temporary route to failover pool in us-east-1 for pra1 traffic 3) collect tcpdump/klog from affected proxies

oncall-sre: I'm oncall and will execute. Throttling LB now (reducing per-connection concurrency):
```
# aws-lb update-target-group --target-group-arn arn:aws:tg:pra1 --deregistration-delay 30 --max-connections 3000
# curl -X POST https://infra/api/lb/throttle -d '{"region":"pra1","concurrency":2000}'
```

ops-bot: action acknowledged — LB throttle applied to pra1 by oncall-sre at 15:26 UTC.

Amol: collecting `kubectl -n edge get pods -o wide` output from pra1 cluster:
```
NAME                             READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   IP             NODE
edge-proxy-7f8d9c6-ptz42         2/2     Running   0          5d    10.2.3.45      pra1-n2
edge-proxy-7f8d9c6-jkq11         2/2     CrashLoop 5          3d    10.2.3.67      pra1-n1
edge-proxy-7f8d9c6-xzq99         1/2     Running   1          17h   10.2.3.89      pra1-n3
```

Kate (SRE): there's a CrashLoop on one replica and degraded readiness on another. Are image pulls or config changes recent?

Amol: no image change. Logs show repeated upstream dial timeouts and a surge of connection resets from the router (TCP RST). Pasting snippet: 
```
[edge-proxy] 2026-03-15T15:12:34Z upstream dial tcp 10.1.8.12:443: i/o timeout
[edge-proxy] 2026-03-15T15:12:34Z upstream connection reset after keepalive
[edge-proxy] 2026-03-15T15:12:36Z closing connection: exceeded in-flight
```

Devon (Platform): I can flip routing for a subset of traffic to us-east-1. Recommend canary 10% to start, ramp if errors drop. Any objections?

Nora (Customer Success): start the canary asap — we should notify impacted customers before larger shifts. I'll draft an outbound note for the flagged tickets.

oncall-sre: initiating canary routing at 15:35 UTC. Command:
```
# infra route set --from pra1 --to use1 --percent 10 --reason "pra1 edge 5xx surge"
```

ops-bot: route update applied (10% pra1->use1) by oncall-sre.

Kate (SRE): monitoring metrics after canary: within 3 minutes, error-rate on canary traffic = 0.3%, pra1 remaining traffic = 5.9% (was 6.8%). Good sign. Keep canary.

Maria (Support): customer #12345 reports temporary improvement post-canary. They still see some timeouts but less frequent.

Amol: digging deeper — kernel keepalive jitter looks suspicious. On pra1 nodes with RSTs, the conntrack table shows leak and a spike in TIME_WAIT. Could be NAT exhaustion on egress NAT gateway.

Devon (Platform): checking cloud NAT metrics — SNAT port usage for pra1 NAT GW-A at 15:20 = 98% used, error increases agree. NAT GW-B is healthy at 26%. Looks like uneven SNAT distribution.

Kate (SRE): mitigation options: 1) scale out NAT or swap to another NAT gateway 2) shift more traffic to failover region 3) restart affected edge-proxy pods to clear conntrack — but that may drop in-flight requests.

oncall-sre: I'll scale NAT out first. k8s restart as last resort. Scaling NAT now.

ops-bot: NAT gw scaled +2 for pra1 at 15:45 UTC. Expected stabilization within 2m.

Kate (SRE): after NAT scale, pra1 error-rate dropped to 2.1% at 15:48. Canary still healthy. Keep monitoring and plan full 50% shift if trend continues.

Nora (Customer Success): sending note to impacted customers: "We are actively mitigating a regional networking issue in the Prairies region; we have shifted part of your traffic to a healthy region and are seeing improvements. We'll update in 30 minutes or sooner." :email:

Maria (Support): updating tickets #12345, #12346 and setting severity to S2.

Devon (Platform): scaling canary to 35% now to relieve pra1.
```
infra route set --from pra1 --to use1 --percent 35 --reason "reduce pra1 NAT pressure"
```

ops-bot: route update applied (35% pra1->use1).

Amol: seeing further drop — pra1 error rate at 0.9% after ramp to 35%. Still some pods with degraded readiness, but overall success.

Kate (SRE): action summary so far: LB throttle applied, NAT scaled, canary routing to us-east ramped to 35%, customer comms sent. Postmortem owner needed.

Nora (Customer Success): prepping post-incident comms once we stabilize. cc: product and legal for any enterprise customers.

Maria (Support): are we capturing packet captures from affected nodes for root cause?

Amol: yes — we have tcpdump from two nodes and conntrack dumps. Uploading to private bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/pra1/1767778001/

oncall-sre: I'm going to handoff to the overnight oncall at 16:10 UTC. Leaving detailed notes in the incident channel and runbook pinned. Handoff checklist: 
- current error rate 0.6%
- canary 35% pra1->use1
- NAT scaled +2 (monitor SNAT usage)
- pods: one CrashLoop — keep restarted but do not mass-restart
- customer tickets updated
- postmortem owner: Amol (will own RCA)

Kate (SRE): ack handoff. I'll stay briefly for context. Assigning pager: oncall-night.

ops-bot: pager assigned to oncall-night at 16:10 UTC.

Amol: I'll own the postmortem and dig into why SNAT distribution skewed so heavily to GW-A and why kernel keepalive tweak correlated with the timing. Suspect NAT session affinity and kube-proxy hazard.

Nora (Customer Success): I'll follow up with impacted customers tomorrow morning local time with a summary and next-steps.

Maria (Support): closing this thread for active mitigation; will reopen if errors spike >1.5% again. Great quick work everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS — mitigated -> monitoring. Severity now S2 (degraded). Postmortem assigned to Amol.

Kate (SRE): postmortem doc: https://gl.redwood.internal/ops/incidents/1767778001 (please add logs, timeline, and proposed fixes).

oncall-sre: handing off. Ping me if anything regresses.

Amol: will upload analysis and timeline by EOD. Thanks all.
